meta.note: Curated by hand from public pages; every entry lists sources with dates. Re-verify entries older than 180 days (publisher_scout.py check).
meta.base_rates_source: per-pitch chance for a good-fit pitch [STIMA]: anchored on Raw Fury (< 1 % of 1,500+ pitches a year) and Outersloth (~1.4 % signing rate); medium/low are skill estimates [OPINIONE]

industry_facts.fact: Hooded Horse contracts: developers keep 65 % of all revenue; at least $100k of localization and marketing per project.
Wholesome Games Presents does marketing and biz-dev, usually no funding or QA, and takes a smaller revenue share than average.

Study of 30 indie contracts: with no advance developers averaged 71% revenue share; with an advance the dev share drops and recoup clauses are near-universal. Example 'good' deal: 60/40 to publisher while recouping a $318k advance, then 60/40 to developer.

Rami Ismail (2026): most common post-recoup split is ~50/50 +/-10%; before recoup 0/100 (dev gets nothing) is increasingly common; publishers recoup the advance plus service costs (marketing, localisation, QA).
Outersloth fund: ~1.4% signing rate; 50% of revenue until recoup, then 15% (~7 years); developer keeps IP.
WINGS Interactive: 50/50 until 1x recoup, then 15% to WINGS; developer keeps IP.
No More Robots (Aug 2024): only very cheap or very expensive pitches get signed now; mid budgets rejected; $400k is too much for NMR.
Ravenage CEO: the first five slides of a pitch deck usually decide whether a game fits.
Inactive/closed publishers 2024-2025 per directory: Humble Games, Versus Evil, Merge Games, Private Division, Firestoke (Aug 2025), Modern Wolf, PID Games (no releases since Dec 2024).
Silver Lining Interactive's Silver Bullet incubator offered indie devs up to $100,000 funding plus publishing, marketing, QA and porting.
Raw Fury receives 1,500+ pitches a year and signs less than 1% (under 0.5% in 2021), not counting games their scouts seek out.

Lawyer Kellen Voyer's review of 30 non-mobile indie publishing contracts (GDC 2020): average advance USD 318k (100k-2M among deals with an advance); average split 60% dev / 40% publisher; 71% dev in no-advance deals, 55% dev in advance deals; 37-42% use full-stop recoup (dev gets 0 until the advance is repaid); average term ~6.8 years, ~49% auto-renew.
Future Friends Games publishes its terms: 80/20 after recoup with no funding, 70/30 after recoup with up to GBP 100k, or 50/50 from day one; marketing spend not recouped.

2024 Steam data (GameDiscoverCo + Gamalytic, games > USD 500): median publisher-backed game USD 16,222 vs USD 3,285 self-published; published games 4x more likely to reach USD 200k+. Selection effect unclear (publishers pick better games).
Zukowski: publishers quickly reject games already in Early Access that need money to reach 1.0, because their model is built around promoting the launch.
Zukowski (Unity Q&A, ~Feb 2025): in 2023, 55.5% of the top Steam games had a publisher.

GameDiscoverCo (2026): with USD 500k of publisher money only ~0.6% of January releases would have recouped; with a USD 100k self-published budget only 6.5% break even. The business works for publishers with strong catalogs or small low-budget teams that make something notable.
Graffiti Games' pitch form asks current wishlists, 3 comparable games, budget and time to finish, and a pitch deck: traction is part of the screening.
Rami Ismail on new publishers (2022): make sure the upfront is 130%+ of a well-paid, comfortable budget.
PlayWay usually requires an ownership stake in the studios it works with and largely dictates which games get made.

Common trap: recoup only from the developer's share; with a USD 500k advance and 50/50, the game must make USD 1M net before the developer sees royalties. Marketing, QA and localization are often recoupable.
Italian games tax credit (MiC/DGCA): 25% of eligible costs, up to EUR 1M a year; only companies with ATECO 62 or 58.2 and share capital/net equity >= EUR 10k; individuals excluded.
